Systematic Review Outlines Artificial Intelligence Strategies for Designing Functional Taste Peptides

A systematic review synthesizes how artificial intelligence-driven prediction platforms and precision regulation strategies can accelerate the development of taste peptides for functional foods. Although taste peptides connect sensory pleasure with bioactivity, their industrial translation remains hindered by empirical screening bottlenecks and a limited understanding of peptide behavior inside complex food systems.

To address traditional trial-and-error screening limitations, researchers evaluate emerging computational models that enable rational, high-throughput peptide design across diverse taste modalities. These artificial intelligence platforms represent a shift toward predictive screening methodologies for identifying targeted tastants.

The review also evaluates how dynamic oral physiological environments and complex food matrix components modulate gustatory transduction and signaling efficacy. To bridge basic sensory perception and industrial processing, the authors detail targeted modulation strategies aimed at amplifying desirable taste profiles and suppressing off-flavors.

Finally, the authors highlight the translational opportunities of dual-functional peptides in precision nutrition, specialized diets for the elderly, and sodium and sugar reduction efforts. Integrating artificial intelligence screening, taste transduction mechanisms, and practical modulation provides strategic guidance for applying taste peptides in functional food products.

In examining computational screening methods, the systematic review highlights how cutting edge artificial intelligence platforms attempt to overcome persistent empirical discovery bottlenecks. Traditional discovery of taste peptides has relied on trial and error screening, an approach constrained by limited efficiency across diverse taste modalities. By synthesizing predictive computational frameworks, the authors outline a shift toward rational and high throughput design. These artificial intelligence platforms focus on predicting peptide behavior, providing a structured approach to identify candidate molecules that link sensory pleasure with biological activity.

Beyond initial identification, the evaluation examines how physical environments shape sensory response. The authors critically review evidence showing that dynamic oral physiological environments and complex food matrix components profoundly modulate gustatory transduction and signaling efficacy. Understanding these matrix interactions is necessary because molecular behavior in food systems directly affects sensory reception. To bridge fundamental perception with industrial application, the review outlines precision modulation strategies. These systematic strategies focus directly on amplifying desirable tastes while suppressing off flavors to support targeted functional food product development.

Finally, the review explores the immense translational potential of dual functional peptides across targeted health applications. The authors evaluate opportunities in precision nutrition, specialized diets for elderly populations, and reformulation initiatives aimed at sodium and sugar reduction. By connecting artificial intelligence discovery platforms, taste transduction mechanisms, environmental influencing factors, and practical regulation strategies, the review establishes a comprehensive synthesis. These insights provide definitive strategic guidance to accelerate the targeted development and health oriented application of dual functional taste peptides across the functional food industry.

Subject of Research: Systematic review of AI-assisted discovery and precision regulation of taste peptides

Article Title: Intelligent discovery and precision regulation of taste peptides: a systematic review from taste mechanisms to health applications

Article References: Cui, Y., Yang, W., Guo, K., Wang, Q., Li, X., Gu, Y., & Wang, Y. (2026). Intelligent discovery and precision regulation of taste peptides: a systematic review from taste mechanisms to health applications. npj Science of Food. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41538-026-01100-2
